title: Majestic Shield
reviewNotes: Reconstructed the seven-piece position after ...g2. Checked Ne4 queen counterattack, queen replacement, Nc4 discovered attack, actual stalemate after Qxd1, and mates after both illustrated king retreats. Corrected automatic captions Na4 to visually displayed Ne4; first retained image contains a dragged piece and was not used as a FEN.
transcript: The genius of white comes up with a knight to f6, sacrificing the knight completely. But of course, if the knight is taken, [music] this would be completely winning after queen to d3 check, picking up the g pawn, and now having a red carpet for the other pawn to promote. But black is not that naive and is not just going to mindlessly capture this knight. Instead, he can just ignore it and push the pawn that is only one step away from getting another queen. And at first glance, it seems like white is completely doomed. There is no way to stop the black pawn from promoting. And although that might be true, white doesn't necessarily have to stop the pawn. Instead, he can counterattack the black queen with knight to a4. Because of course, if black promotes, he would be able to pick up the queen, and this would still allow him to promote the pawn. But black is a powerful and brilliant foe, and he finds the incredible counter brilliancy. Queen takes d5, giving up the only piece left he has, seemingly for nothing. But actually, this is a better chance for black to draw the game because now of course, he can just get another queen. And queen and knight versus queen is very often just [music] a draw. And after knight to d2, preparing a checkmate in one on b3, black plays the mysterious queen to d1. Of course, this move defends checkmate in one, but it also kind of looks like a blunder because it allows knight to c4 check with a discover attack on the black queen. Incredibly, white cannot touch the black queen because out of nowhere, this would be a stalemate and a draw. So, is black simply out of the woods in this position? Well, not exactly because white knows about Chess Shield. The way to defeat Doom Scrolling is by replacing it with chess practice. And Chess Shield will block all of the apps that you think are distracting you from practicing chess until you study some puzzles. And since many of you asked, I am glad to announce that Chess Shield is finally out on Android. But getting back to the game, the way for white to finally put the last nail in this coffin is the very precise queen to G2 check. There is no way for the black queen to block the check without being captured. And no matter where this king moves, on the next move queen to B2 is going to be a beautiful checkmate. You can find more info about Chess Shield in the pinned comment.
